title: Projectives Standard Filtrations and Bgg Reciprocity

items.title: Truncation at a finitely generated downward weight ideal
items.statement: Fix a finite set S of weights and I=union_{nu in S}(nu-Q+). O^I consists of objects with support in I. A finite ideal of simple labels in a fixed finite linkage block is a different, finite poset notion. O^{<=nu} uses S={nu}; its weight ideal is generally infinite.

references.title: Lecture 8, Lemma 4.10 proof pp.7–8 (support truncation made explicit)

items.title: A maximal-weight Verma is projective in its truncation
items.statement: If nu is maximal in I and nu-Q+ is contained in I, Delta(nu) is projective in O^I. It is also projective in O whenever no label in its linkage block is strictly above nu.
items.proof_strategy: Weight evaluation Hom(Delta(nu),X)=X_nu is exact when no higher weight occurs. In a block use finite length, highest-weight simple factors, and support; exact block projection extends projectivity to O.

items.title: Exact block projections preserve projectives
items.statement: Projection to a generalized central-character summand or linkage block is exact and both adjoint to its exact inclusion; it preserves projectives.

references.title: Lecture 8, Lemma 4.10 and proof of Theorem 4.3 pp.7–8

items.proof_strategy: Decompose morphisms into summands. Hom from the projected object into a block object equals Hom from the original object; apply exactness.

items.title: Finite-dimensional tensor adjunction and projectivity
items.statement: For a finite-dimensional g-module E, tensoring by the ordinary dual E* is both adjoint to tensoring by E on O; consequently E tensor P is projective if P is projective in O. No assertion about tensoring within a fixed truncation.

references.title: Lecture 9 Lemma 3.3 and its proof pp.4–5

items.proof_strategy: Write evaluation and coevaluation, check g-equivariance and the two triangle identities. The right adjoint is exact.

items.title: Finite Borel induction generators
items.statement: For n>=1, let E(nu,n)=U(b)/(U(b){h-nu(h)}+U(b)(n+)^n), with (n+)^n denoting products of n positive-root operators, and G(nu,n)=U(g) tensor_{U(b)} E(nu,n).

items.title: Block projections of finite induction generators represent weights
items.statement: E(nu,n) is finite dimensional and a weight b-module. G(nu,n) lies in O. For each central character chi, sufficiently large n makes pr_chi G(nu,n) represent X -> X_nu on O_chi.

references.title: Lecture 8 Lemma 4.10 pp.7–8; do not use the incorrect root-tuple direct-sum formula in footnote 7

items.proof_strategy: PBW bounds monomials modulo the n-th augmentation power. A map is a weight-nu vector annihilated by that power. All objects of O_chi have support in the finite union of cones below its finite dot-orbit labels, giving a uniform n independent of X.

items.title: Category O has enough projectives
items.statement: Every O-object is a quotient of a projective object in O; each simple admits a projective epimorphism in its block.

references.title: Lecture 8 Theorem 4.3 proof p.8; Etingof §16.2 p.85

items.proof_strategy: The representing object is projective because weight evaluation is exact and maps onto L(nu). For an extension of two objects, lift the projective cover of the quotient and combine it with a projective epimorphism to the subobject. Induct on length.

items.title: Dominant integral-subsystem weights are maximal in linkage
items.statement: If <nu+rho,alpha^vee> is not a negative integer for any positive root, no label in W_nu dot nu is strictly above nu. For every mu, nu=mu+N rho satisfies this condition for sufficiently large integer N.

references.title: §16.1 Corollary 16.1 p.84; integral-reflection formulation, not a root-lattice-coset stabilizer identification

items.proof_strategy: Prove the reflection-closed integral roots form a finite root system with inherited positive system. The real component of nu+rho is dominant for it and the orthogonal component is fixed. The reduced-word positive-root calculation gives w dot nu<=nu. Finally shift each integral pairing upward using rho.

items.title: Enough projectives by finite-dimensional tensoring
items.statement: For each mu there is nu=mu+N rho and finite-dimensional E such that E* tensor Delta(nu) is projective and surjects onto L(mu).
items.proof_strategy: Take E=L(N rho). Its highest vector tensored with that of L(mu) gives a nonzero map Delta(nu)->E tensor L(mu), and tensor adjunction gives a nonzero, hence surjective, map to L(mu). Block-project if desired. This route remains blocked by the finite-dimensional supplier finding.

items.title: Essential projective epimorphisms in O
items.statement: A projective cover of X is a projective epimorphism P -> X such that no proper subobject of P still surjects onto X.

items.title: Fitting decomposition for finite-length objects
items.statement: For an endomorphism f of an O-object, sufficiently large n gives M=ker f^n direct-sum im f^n. If M is indecomposable, f is invertible or nilpotent and End(M) is local.

references.title: Lecture 8 Appendix A Lemma A.1 p.9

items.proof_strategy: Stabilize kernels and images by finite length; their intersection is zero and their lengths add to length M. For indecomposable M one summand vanishes. If f is not a unit it is nilpotent, so 1-f is a unit; use the local-ring criterion.

items.title: Existence and uniqueness of indecomposable projective covers
items.statement: Every L(lambda) has a cover P(lambda), unique up to a generally nonunique isomorphism over L(lambda). It is indecomposable with local endomorphism algebra, a unique maximal submodule, and Hom(P(lambda),L(mu)) of dimension delta_lambda,mu.

references.title: Lecture 8 Theorem 4.4 and Appendix A pp.6–9

items.proof_strategy: Minimize length among projective epimorphisms; a minimal subobject still surjecting splits off by projective lifting and finite length. This proves essentiality. Lift between covers in both directions. Fitting gives locality; the sum of two distinct maximal kernels would split the identity into two nonunits. End(L)=C follows on its highest line.

items.title: Projective covers lift onto standards
items.statement: The map P(lambda)->L(lambda) lifts to a surjection P(lambda)->Delta(lambda).
items.proof_strategy: Lift by projectivity. Its image is not contained in the unique maximal Verma submodule, so contains the highest line and is the whole Verma module.

items.title: Finite Verma flags
items.statement: A Verma flag is a finite filtration 0=F0 subset ... subset Fr=X with factors Delta(mu_i). Initially write the count with the flag as an argument; the following lemma permits notation (X:Delta(mu)).

references.title: Lecture 9 Theorem-Definition 1.1 p.1 and Proposition-Definition 2.1 p.4

items.title: Verma multiplicities do not depend on the flag
items.statement: The number of occurrences of each Delta(mu) in a finite Verma flag is independent of the flag.
items.proof_strategy: Add classes along the filtration and use linear independence of standard classes in K0(O).

items.title: Tensor identity and ordered Verma flags
items.statement: For a finite-dimensional weight b-module F, induction is exact and has the flag induced from a one-dimensional b-flag of F. For finite-dimensional g-module E, E tensor Delta(nu) has a Verma flag containing Delta(nu+eta) exactly dim E_eta times, ordered with larger weights first.

references.title: Lecture 9 Lemma 1.5 pp.1–2 and Lemma 3.5 p.5

items.proof_strategy: Use freeness of U(g) as right U(b)-module. Prove induction tensor identity with coproduct and antipode maps; order weights of E from maximal downwards to obtain the b-flag.

items.title: Peeling a maximal-weight Verma from a flag
items.statement: If X has a Verma flag and 0!=v in X_nu where nu is maximal in supp X, the induced Delta(nu)->X is injective and its quotient has a Verma flag with one fewer factor.

references.title: Lecture 9 Lemma 1.6 p.2; maximal support weight is essential

items.proof_strategy: Choose the first flag term containing the cyclic image. Projection to that factor is nonzero; maximality forces its highest weight to equal nu, so the projection is an isomorphism. Splice the remaining filtration.

items.title: Verma flags pass to direct summands
items.statement: If X=X1 direct-sum X2 has a finite Verma flag, both summands have finite Verma flags.
items.proof_strategy: Induct on the flag length. A maximal support vector has a nonzero component in one summand; peel its Verma, then apply induction to (X1/Delta) direct-sum X2.

items.title: Projectives in O have finite Verma flags
items.statement: Every projective O-object has a finite Verma flag. For P(lambda), the restriction to labels mu>=lambda follows below from reciprocity, without being assumed in its proof.
items.proof_strategy: Finite weight generators give a surjection from a finite sum of G(nu,n), each Verma-filtered by the Borel flag lemma. A projective quotient splits; use summand closure. No freeness-implies-flag assumption.

items.title: Hom from a projective cover counts composition factors
items.statement: For M in O, dim Hom(P(lambda),M)=[M:L(lambda)].

references.title: Lecture 8 Corollary 4.9 p.7; Etingof Proposition 16.2(ii) pp.85–86

items.proof_strategy: Exact Hom adds dimensions along a finite composition series; its value on simple factors is the Kronecker delta.

items.title: Restricted duality supplies enough injectives
items.statement: D(P(lambda)) is an injective hull of L(lambda); every O-object embeds into an injective object.

references.title: Lecture 8 Theorem 4.3 p.6 and proof p.8

items.proof_strategy: Dualize projective epimorphisms and essentiality using the exact involution. This precedes balanced Ext.

items.title: Standard-costandard Hom and Ext-one orthogonality
items.statement: Hom(Delta(mu),nabla(nu)) has dimension delta_mu,nu, and Ext^1_O(Delta(mu),nabla(nu))=0 for all weights, including equal or incomparable weights.
items.proof_strategy: Hom is the dual of the highest-weight quotient of U(n-). In an extension lift the top as a weight vector when mu is not strictly below nu; it is singular. In the remaining case dualize and apply the first case. Invoke Yoneda/derived comparison only after enough projectives and injectives are available. Work in ZFC with supplied resolutions. Extension classes form a set: split the underlying vector-space sequence and encode every middle action on the fixed vector space nabla(nu) direct-sum Delta(mu); the compatible g-actions and endpoint maps form a set, then quotient by extension equivalence.

items.title: Hom to costandards counts flag multiplicities
items.statement: For Verma-filtered X, dim Hom(X,nabla(mu))=(X:Delta(mu)); also Ext^1(X,nabla(mu))=0.
items.proof_strategy: Apply the first-variable long exact sequence successively to flag extensions; the Ext-one term vanishes by induction.

items.title: BGG reciprocity
items.statement: For arbitrary complex highest weights lambda,mu, (P(lambda):Delta(mu))=[Delta(mu):L(lambda)].
items.proof_strategy: Count Hom(P(lambda),nabla(mu)) in two ways; restricted duality fixes each simple and preserves finite composition multiplicities.

items.title: The triangular restriction on projective flags
items.statement: In P(lambda) only Delta(mu) with mu>=lambda occur, and (P(lambda):Delta(lambda))=1.

references.title: Lecture 9 Theorem 2.2 with standard highest-weight support

items.proof_strategy: Use highest-weight support and the one-dimensional top of Delta(lambda). This is a consequence, not an input to reciprocity.

items.title: Injectives have costandard filtrations
items.statement: Every injective O-object has a finite costandard filtration. For I(lambda)=D(P(lambda)), (I(lambda):nabla(mu))=[Delta(mu):L(lambda)].

references.title: Lecture 9 Theorem-Definition 1.2 and Theorem 1.4 p.1, Theorem 2.2 p.4

items.proof_strategy: Duality exchanges projective and injective objects and reverses finite flags.

items.title: Kernels of epimorphisms between standardly filtered objects
items.statement: In 0->K->M->N->0 with N Verma-filtered, M is Verma-filtered iff K is.
items.proof_strategy: Reduce to N a Verma. Peel a maximal standard from M; its projection to N is zero or an isomorphism. Use induction in the former case and splitting in the latter.

items.title: Ext orthogonality characterizes Verma flags
items.statement: For X in O, a finite Verma flag is equivalent to Ext^1(X,nabla(mu))=0 for all mu, and to Ext^i(X,nabla(mu))=0 for all mu and i>0.
items.proof_strategy: First dimension shift along a projective epimorphism onto each standard; its kernel has a flag. For converse use the image Z of the top-weight Verma sum in X and Y=X/Z. Exact Hom into the maximal costandard shows Ext1(Y,nabla)=0, then induction gives its flag and Ext2 vanishing. Deduce Ext1(Z,nabla)=0 and the kernel of the top Verma sum has no maps to any costandard; a nonzero finite-length kernel would have a simple quotient embedding into a costandard.

items.title: Translation by tensoring and projection
items.statement: For finite-dimensional E define T_{chi,E,psi}(X)=pr_psi(E tensor X). For integral weights lambda,mu, set T_lambda^mu using E=L(eta), where eta is the dominant W-conjugate of mu-lambda. Labels denote highest weights, not rho-shifted parameters.

items.title: Translation is exact and biadjoint
items.statement: T_{chi,E,psi} is exact and both adjoint to T_{psi,E*,chi}. For integral lambda,mu this identifies the reversed translation. For finite-dimensional simple E, translation commutes with restricted duality up to a chosen self-duality isomorphism.
items.proof_strategy: Compose block adjunctions and tensor adjunction. For reversed translation identify the highest weight of E* from its lowest weight. Restricted duality D(E)=E is not ordinary E*=E.

items.title: Dot-Weyl facets and single-wall data
items.statement: On the real weight space, facets have fixed signs of <lambda+rho,alpha^vee>. Fix integral dot-antidominant lambda,mu with lambda regular, mu in its chamber closure and dot stabilizer {1,s_alpha}. The wall formulas below use these hypotheses.

items.title: The weight-exclusion lemma for translation into a facet closure
items.statement: For integral lambda and mu in the closure of its dot facet, put nu=mu-lambda and let E have highest weight the dominant conjugate of nu. If gamma is a weight of E and lambda+gamma is in W dot mu, then gamma=nu, an extremal weight of multiplicity one.
items.proof_strategy: Use the complete chamber-distance induction in Humphreys §7.5: reflect across a separating wall, keep the adjusted weight in a root string, and strictly reduce distance. The extremal-weight endpoint forces zero wall pairing and then gamma=nu. Requires the prerequisite weight-geometry package recorded as fatal in notes.

items.title: Translation to and from a single wall on standards
items.statement: With the integral dot-antidominant single-wall data, T_lambda^mu Delta(w dot lambda)=Delta(w dot mu). Translation back has a two-term flag with factors Delta(w dot lambda), Delta(ws dot lambda), each once; its larger highest weight occurs as the submodule. More generally the return multiplicities are indexed by the quotient of dot stabilizers.
items.proof_strategy: Into the wall keep the single tensor weight. Back out, the tensor flag and block projection give a flag; compute each multiplicity by adjunction and standard-costandard Hom. It is one exactly for labels in the stabilizer coset. Use the ordered tensor flag for the two-factor orientation.

title: Projectives Standard Filtrations and Bgg Reciprocity — Examples

items.title: The two projectives in the principal sl2 block
items.statement: With h-weights 0,-2, P(0)=Delta(0); P(-2) has nonsplit exact sequence 0->Delta(0)->P(-2)->Delta(-2)->0. Its simple head and socle are L(-2), with middle L(0).

references.title: Lecture 9 Theorem 2.2 p.4 and Example 3.16 p.7

items.proof_strategy: Compute the two Verma composition series from ef^k v=k(l-k+1)f^{k-1}v. Reciprocity determines flags; the unique simple head excludes splitting. The contained Delta(0) has socle L(-2). A further simple submodule outside it would map isomorphically onto the simple quotient Delta(-2) and split the sequence; one inside it is already in that socle.

items.title: The sl2 reciprocity matrices
items.statement: Order labels (0,-2). Rows Delta and columns L give D=[[1,1],[0,1]]; rows P and columns Delta give F=[[1,0],[1,1]]=transpose(D).

references.title: Lecture 9 Theorem 2.2 p.4; explicit rank-one calculation

items.proof_strategy: Specify both indexing conventions and read the entries from the calculated composition series and flags.

items.title: Translation through the sl2 wall
items.statement: Tensor with L(1) and project: T_0^{-1} sends Delta(0) and Delta(-2) to Delta(-1), kills L(0), and sends L(-2) to L(-1). T_{-1}^0 Delta(-1)=P(-2).
items.proof_strategy: The singular Verma is simple and projective. Adjunction counts the simple head of its translated projective and identifies P(-2); compute the tensor flag and the two-weight tensor directly.

items.title: The antidominant sl2 Verma need not be projective
items.statement: Delta(-2)=L(-2) is not projective in its regular block: P(-2)->Delta(-2) is a nonsplit epimorphism. Delta(0), the dominant Verma, is projective in O.

references.title: Lecture 9 Theorem 2.2 with sl2 computation; Etingof Proposition 16.4 p.86

items.proof_strategy: A projective quotient would split its displayed projective epimorphism, contradicting indecomposability.

items.title: A projective Verma flag need not split
items.statement: The flag 0 subset Delta(0) subset P(-2) is not a direct-sum decomposition.
items.proof_strategy: A split sum would have simple quotients L(0) and L(-2), contrary to the unique head of P(-2).

items.title: A quotient of a Verma-filtered object need not have a Verma flag
items.statement: In sl2, Delta(0) and its submodule Delta(-2) have Verma flags, while their quotient L(0) does not.
items.proof_strategy: Every nonzero Verma has infinite vector dimension; a finite Verma filtration cannot yield the one-dimensional trivial module.

items.title: The same Verma in two ambient categories
items.statement: Delta(-2) is projective in O^{<=-2} but not in the full regular sl2 block.

references.title: §16.3 Proposition 16.4 proof p.86, applied to a support truncation

items.proof_strategy: Compare exact weight evaluation in the truncation with the nonsplit epimorphism whose middle term has weight zero outside that truncation.
